Wheeling

the Ohio Valley & the National Road — Washington PA to Zanesville

35 places · 28 sights · 7 to eat & drink · 5 areas · 39 sources · status last checked 2026-08-27

Wheeling, WV 11

downtown, Centre Market, Oglebay, Wheeling Island

  1. Must see · Wheeling, WV

    Wheeling Suspension Bridge

    The oldest major long-span suspension bridge in the world still carrying traffic. Built by Charles Ellet Jr. in 1849 (1010 ft, then the world's longest); rebuilt 1856 after a tornado, stay cables later added to a Washington Roebling design. NRHP 1970, ASCE National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark, National Historic Landmark 1976.

    Look for ARCH

    1010 Main St over the Ohio River (US-40), Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by e-WV: The West Virginia Encyclopedia, Asce, Wikipedia (notability / history)

  2. Must see · Wheeling, WV

    West Virginia Independence Hall

    The birthplace of West Virginia and a National Historic Landmark. Built 1859-60 as a federal custom house; site of the Wheeling Conventions and first WV Constitutional Convention that made the state during the Civil War. Restored museum, free tours Tue-Sat.

    Look for HIST

    1528 Market St, Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by WV Dept. of Arts, Culture & History, WV Tourism (Almost Heaven), Wikipedia (notability / history)

  3. Must see · Wheeling, WV

    Centre Market Historic District

    Historic market district anchored by the 1853 Centre Market house, the oldest cast-iron market house in the country (older than the state itself). Two market buildings plus a walkable block of antique shops, eateries and salons; monthly First Friday events. NRHP historic district.

    Look for MKT

    2200 Market St, Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by WV Tourism (Almost Heaven), Wikipedia (notability / history), Visit Wheeling WV (CVB)

  4. Must see · Italian & Pizza · Wheeling, WV

    Figaretti's Restaurant

    A 2026 James Beard America's Classics winner; family-run since 1948 from Anna Figaretti's garage-made sauce, and previously named the best Italian restaurant in West Virginia.

    1035 Mount de Chantal Rd, Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation (America's Classics), The Intelligencer / Wheeling News-Register, West Virginia Public Broadcasting

  5. Must see · Wheeling, WV

    Oglebay Resort & Park

    1,700-acre municipal resort on industrialist Earl Oglebay's former estate. Home to the Good Zoo (WV's only AZA-accredited zoo), the Carriage House Glass Museum (3,000+ pieces of Wheeling glass incl. the 5-ft Sweeney Punch Bowl), the Mansion Museum, gardens, golf, and the winter Festival of Lights (300+ acres, 1M+ lights).

    Look for PARK

    465 Lodge Dr, Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by Oglebay Resort & Park (official), WV Tourism (Almost Heaven)

  6. Worth the detour · Wheeling, WV

    Capitol Theatre

    Restored 1928 downtown theatre and full entertainment complex; home of the Wheeling Symphony Orchestra and host to touring Broadway, comedy and concert acts (Jerry Seinfeld, Willie Nelson).

    Look for MUS

    1928 Market St, Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by Visit Wheeling WV (CVB), WV Tourism (Almost Heaven)

  7. Worth the detour · Wheeling, WV

    Kruger Street Toy & Train Museum

    Tens of thousands of toys and trains housed in a restored 1906 Victorian schoolhouse, with a 2,000+ sq ft operating model-train layout, rotating exhibits and guided tours. A family favorite.

    Look for FAM

    144 Kruger St, Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by Visit Wheeling WV (CVB), WV Tourism (Almost Heaven)

  8. Worth the detour · Wheeling, WV

    Wheeling Heritage Trail

    About 13.5 miles of paved rail-trail on former railroad beds, looping through the city and along the Ohio River for walking and cycling.

    Look for PARK

    Riverfront trailheads along the Ohio River, Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by WV Tourism (Almost Heaven), Visit Wheeling WV (CVB)

  9. Deep cut · Wheeling, WV

    Monument Place (Shepherd Hall)

    Stone plantation house built 1798 by Moses Shepherd on the old National Road, later renamed Monument Place. NRHP-listed. Owned by the Osiris Shrine Temple; interior access is limited (events/appointment) rather than a regular public museum.

    Look for HIST

    91 Kruger St, Elm Grove, Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability / history), Weelunk (Wheeling culture site), Saharchipedia

  10. Deep cut · Wheeling, WV

    Oglebay Institute's Stifel Fine Arts Center

    "Edemar," a 1910-14 Classical Revival mansion given to the Oglebay Institute in 1976 and run as an arts center with galleries, exhibitions and classes. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places (1992).

    Look for MUS

    1330 National Rd, Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by WV Tourism (Almost Heaven), Wikipedia (notability / history)

  11. Deep cut · Wheeling, WV

    Wheeling Island Historic District

    A large residential island in the Ohio River with 1,110+ contributing buildings in Italianate, Queen Anne and Craftsman styles; NRHP historic district (1992). Also home to the Wheeling Island racetrack and casino.

    Look for MKT

    Wheeling Island (across the Suspension Bridge), Wheeling, WV 26003

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability / history), WV Tourism (Almost Heaven)

Washington, PA 8

Washington & Jefferson, LeMoyne House

  1. Must see · Washington, PA

    Meadowcroft Rockshelter & Historic Village

    A National Historic Landmark rock overhang holding evidence of human habitation ~16,000-19,000 years ago — the oldest known site of human habitation in North America. Operated by the Heinz History Center; interpretive villages (16th-c. Indian village, 18th-c. trading post, 19th-c. village). Seasonal (roughly May-Oct).

    Look for HIST

    401 Meadowcroft Rd, Avella, PA 15312

    Recommended by Heinzhistory, National Trust for Historic Preservation, Uncovering PA

  2. Must see · American & New American · Washington, PA

    Century Inn

    Built 1794 as Hill's Tavern, the oldest continuously operating inn on the National Road; on the National Register, it sheltered Presidents Washington, Jackson and Polk and reopened after a 2015 fire.

    2175 E National Pike (US-40), Scenery Hill, PA 15360

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability / history), ExplorePAHistory (witf), Visit Washington County PA (tourism)

  3. Must see · Washington, PA

    LeMoyne House

    1812 home of abolitionist Dr. F. Julius LeMoyne — Pennsylvania's first National Historic Landmark of the Underground Railroad. LeMoyne also built the Western Hemisphere's first crematory (tourable). Run by the Washington County Historical Society.

    Look for HIST

    49 E Maiden St, Washington, PA 15301

    Recommended by Visit Washington County PA, Washington County Historical Society (PA)

  4. Must see · Washington, PA

    Pennsylvania Trolley Museum

    A ~4-mile scenic round-trip aboard restored streetcars from a collection of nearly 50 cars (PA, WV, OH and beyond), plus a Visitor Education Center with a trolley simulator, exhibits and film. A top family stop.

    Look for FAM

    1 Museum Rd, Washington, PA 15301

    Recommended by Visit Washington County PA, Washington County Historical Society (PA)

  5. Must see · Diners & Breakfast · Washington, PA

    Shorty's Lunch

    A Washington, PA hot-dog lunch counter since the early 1930s, run by the Alexas family; its chili-topped 'everything' dog commands the kind of loyalty most brands only dream of.

    34 W Chestnut St, Washington, PA 15301

    Recommended by Observer-Reporter (Washington, PA), Wikipedia (notability / history)

  6. Worth the detour · Washington, PA

    David Bradford House

    1788 stone townhouse of David Bradford, a leader of the 1794 Whiskey Rebellion. Restored house museum with period furnishings, hand-embroidered wainscot (1773) and a children's room.

    Look for HIST

    175 S Main St, Washington, PA 15301

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability / history), Visit Washington County PA

  7. Worth the detour · Washington, PA

    Washington County Courthouse

    A 1900 Beaux-Arts courthouse by architect Frederick J. Osterling, crowned by a 150-ft dome topped with a statue of George Washington, with a grand central stairway and 40-ft stained-glass ceiling. NRHP 1974; still in use.

    Look for ARCH

    1 S Main St, Washington, PA 15301

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability / history), Observer-Reporter (Washington, PA)

  8. Worth the detour · American & New American · Washington, PA

    The Union Grill

    Opened 1967 and named for the stonemasons and union workers who filled its tavern; a downtown Washington fixture for Italian-American cooking and an Observer-Reporter Best-of-the-Best regular.

    13 E Wheeling St, Washington, PA 15301

    Recommended by Observer-Reporter (Washington, PA), Wikipedia (notability / history)

Ohio Valley 4

St. Clairsville & Belmont County OH

  1. Must see · Ohio Valley

    Blaine Hill "S" Bridge

    Built 1828, the oldest bridge in Ohio and the longest (345 ft) surviving three-arch sandstone "S" bridge on the National Road — the first federally funded highway. Named Ohio's official Bicentennial Bridge in 2003.

    Look for HIST

    Historic National Rd (US-40), Blaine, OH 43909

    Recommended by Federal Highway Administration (Highway History), Visit Belmont County (Ohio), Wikipedia (notability / history)

  2. Must see · Ohio Valley

    Great Stone Viaduct

    A monumental sandstone railroad viaduct (1871) with 43 stone arches — the 37 ring stones symbolize the 37 states of the reunited Union. Built by the B&O/Central Ohio Railroads as the "Great Shortline to the West." NRHP 1976; walking trail opened to the public 2022.

    Look for ARCH

    34th St, Bellaire, OH 43906

    Recommended by Visit Belmont County (Ohio), Ohio.org (TourismOhio)

  3. Worth the detour · Ohio Valley

    Belmont County Victorian Mansion Museum

    A 26-room Romanesque Revival mansion (1888-93, the Bradfield house), formerly the "Gay '90s" museum, filled with period decoration. Open year-round by appointment; especially popular as a holiday destination.

    Look for MUS

    532 N Chestnut St, Barnesville, OH 43713

    Recommended by Belmontmuseum, WTRF 7 News

  4. Deep cut · Ohio Valley

    Dysart Woods

    The largest remaining old-growth forest tract in southeastern Ohio — a 50-acre core of 300-400-year-old oaks (some over 4 ft around) within a 455-acre preserve, the only known remnant mixed-mesophytic forest in Ohio. Hiking trails; part of the Old-Growth Forest Network.

    Look for PARK

    State Route 147, Belmont, OH 43718

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability / history), Old-Growth Forest Network, Visit Belmont County (Ohio)

Cambridge & Guernsey County 4

Dickens Village, Salt Fork

  1. Must see · Cambridge & Guernsey County

    Salt Fork State Park

    Ohio's largest state park — 17,229 acres of land and 2,952 of water, with a lodge, an 18-hole golf course, a 2,500-ft swimming beach, marinas, a nature center and extensive hiking/equestrian trails.

    Look for PARK

    14755 Cadiz Rd, Lore City, OH 43755

    Recommended by Ohiodnr, Wikipedia (notability / history)

  2. Must see · Diners & Breakfast · Cambridge & Guernsey County

    Theo's Restaurant

    Downtown Cambridge on the National Road since 1931 (as Coney Island Lunch), family-run by the Theodosopoulos family since 1963; its coney dogs have been a mainstay for over 90 years.

    632 Wheeling Ave, Cambridge, OH 43725

    Recommended by Visit Guernsey County / Cambridge OH, Explore U.S. 40 (National Road heritage project)

  3. Worth the detour · Cambridge & Guernsey County

    Mosser Glass

    A working handcrafted-pressed-glass factory (40+ years) offering weekday factory-floor tours where you watch artisans press glass, plus a showroom. Factory tours Mon-Fri (morning/early-afternoon windows); showroom Mon-Fri.

    Look for GLASS

    9279 Cadiz Rd, Cambridge, OH 43725

    Recommended by Visit Guernsey County / Cambridge OH, OhioHealth (regional travel blog)

  4. Worth the detour · Cambridge & Guernsey County

    National Museum of Cambridge Glass

    Home of the National Cambridge Collectors, with 10,000+ pieces of the world-famous Cambridge Glass Company's elegant glassware and interactive exhibits. Seasonal: Apr-Oct (Wed-Sun), limited winter hours.

    Look for GLASS

    136 S 9th St, Cambridge, OH 43725

    Recommended by Cambridgeglass, Visit Guernsey County / Cambridge OH

Zanesville & the National Road to the Columbus edge 8

Muskingum, New Concord, Norwich

  1. Must see · Zanesville & the National Road to the Columbus edge

    Zanesville Y-Bridge

    A rare Y-shaped, three-way bridge at the confluence of the Licking and Muskingum Rivers — you can drive onto it and change direction mid-span. Carries US-40 (the National Road); the current span dates to 1902 and is famous enough that pilots recognize it from the air.

    Look for ICON

    Linden Ave at the Muskingum & Licking Rivers (US-40), Zanesville, OH 43701

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability / history), Visit Zanesville-Muskingum County

  2. Must see · Zanesville & the National Road to the Columbus edge

    The Wilds

    A ~10,000-acre wildlife conservation center on reclaimed strip-mine land, run by the Columbus Zoo — rhinos, giraffes, cheetahs and 25+ rare/endangered species roaming in mixed-species pastures. Open-air safaris, zipline, horseback and fishing tours. Seasonal (open daily May-Sept, weekends Oct); reservations required.

    Look for PARK

    14000 International Rd, Cumberland, OH 43732

    Recommended by The Wilds (official, Columbus Zoo), Visit Zanesville-Muskingum County

  3. Must see · Zanesville & the National Road to the Columbus edge

    National Road & Zane Grey Museum

    An Ohio History Connection museum with three galleries: the National Road (America's first federally funded highway), Western novelist Zane Grey (a Zanesville native descended from National Road builder Ebenezer Zane), and Ohio art pottery.

    Look for HIST

    8850 East Pike, Norwich, OH 43767

    Recommended by Ohio History Connection, NSBF

  4. Must see · Ice Cream & Sweets · Zanesville & the National Road to the Columbus edge

    Tom's Ice Cream Bowl

    A Zanesville institution since 1948, named after a customer who demanded his sundae be served in a soup bowl; a USA Today-recognized ice-cream stop known for its Tin Roof sundaes.

    532 McIntire Ave, Zanesville, OH 43701

    Recommended by Ohio.org (TourismOhio), Wikipedia (notability / history)

  5. Worth the detour · Zanesville & the National Road to the Columbus edge

    John & Annie Glenn Museum

    The boyhood home of astronaut and senator John Glenn — the first American to orbit Earth — presented as a costumed living-history tour of 1930s New Concord. Part of the Ohio History Connection system.

    Look for HIST

    72 W Main St, New Concord, OH 43762

    Recommended by Ohio History Connection, Whiz News (Zanesville)

  6. Deep cut · Zanesville & the National Road to the Columbus edge

    Lorena Sternwheeler

    A replica sternwheel riverboat offering sightseeing and dinner excursions on the Muskingum River from Zane's Landing Park at the west end of Market Street. Seasonal cruises.

    Look for FAM

    Zane's Landing Park, N 5th St, Zanesville, OH 43701

    Recommended by Visit Zanesville-Muskingum County, Ohio Traveler

  7. Deep cut · Zanesville & the National Road to the Columbus edge

    Blue Rock State Park

    A quiet 322-acre state park around Cutler Lake, surrounded by 4,573 acres of Blue Rock State Forest, ~11 miles southeast of Zanesville — swimming, fishing, camping and hiking.

    Look for PARK

    7924 Cutler Lake Rd, Blue Rock, OH 43720

    Recommended by Ohiodnr, Wikipedia (notability / history)

  8. Closed — kept for the record · Italian & Pizza · Zanesville & the National Road to the Columbus edge

    Old Market House Inn — CLOSED

    A downtown Zanesville steak-and-Italian mainstay for 51 years; it closed in May 2025 and the Market Street space is being reborn under new ownership as the upscale Market Street Prime.

    424 Market St, Zanesville, OH 43701

    Recommended by Zanesville Times Recorder, Whiz News (Fox Zanesville), Visit Zanesville-Muskingum County

28 sights and 7 places to eat across Wheeling, WV, nearby Washington, PA, and the National Road (I-70) corridor west through eastern Ohio — St. Clairsville, Cambridge and Zanesville — to where the Columbus guide begins. Each is traceable to the source that named it. The valley’s canon is its own: DiCarlo’s Wheeling-style pizza, Coleman’s fish sandwich, WV pepperoni rolls, Zanesville’s Tom’s Ice Cream Bowl, plus the Suspension Bridge, Oglebay, the Y-Bridge and Dickens Village.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. The Ohio Valley’s canon is its own: DiCarlo’s Wheeling-style pizza (cold cheese on a square), the Coleman’s fish sandwich, WV pepperoni rolls, the valley’s deep Italian heritage (Undo’s, Figaretti’s, Ye Olde Alpha), and Zanesville’s Tom’s Ice Cream Bowl & Adornetto’s, sourced to the Wheeling Intelligencer, Weelunk and the Zanesville Times Recorder. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — the Wheeling Intelligencer/News-Register, Weelunk, the Observer-Reporter, the Zanesville Times Recorder, Visit Wheeling WV, Uncovering PA, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
